topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture by framing the learning outcomes on cancer genetics, cellular transformation, and tumor progression.

topics.label: Viral oncogenesis and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for testing transformed phenotypes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and classifications of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the functional definitions and gene-dosage mechanisms of oncogenic and tumor-suppressive mutations in cell cycle control.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how failures in DNA repair pathways and mitotic chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how inherited mutations and acquired genetic alterations drive the stepwise progression of tumors over time.

topics.label: Lecture closing and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: It provides administrative wrap-up, reading recommendations, and an outlook on the next lecture.
